title: Leo: feeling like you again
from December 5
summary: Rahu and Ketu, the north and south nodes, change signs on December 5. What lifts for a Leo Moon that day, what wakes up in your daily work, why rest matters, and how to use the next year and a half.

inside: What Rahu and Ketu, the north and south nodes, are
What lifts for you on December 5 and what begins
How to use the eighteen months that follow, step by step
intro: If you are a Leo by Moon sign, the last year and a half may have felt slightly off. Not bad, exactly, just not quite you. The warmth and confidence you are known for may have come and gone, and the people closest to you may have pulled you in directions you did not choose. On Saturday, December 5, 2026, the two points in the sky that the tradition links to that feeling both change sign at the same moment.

This guide explains what those two points are, what moves off your sign and out of your partnerships that day, what moves into your daily work and your quiet hours, and how long it lasts. Nothing here is a promise. It is what Vedic astrology reads from the sky by your Moon sign, and how to use it well.

sections.label: The two nodes
title: A head that wants,
a tail that lets go.
paragraphs: Rahu and Ketu are not planets you can see. They are the two points where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path, which is why Western astrology calls them the north node and the south node of the Moon. Rahu is the north node and Ketu is the south node. They always sit exactly opposite each other, and they always change sign together.

The tradition pictures them as a dragon cut in two. Rahu is the head with no body: all appetite, always wanting more, never quite full. Wherever he sits, life is read as louder, hungrier and more ambitious. Ketu is the tail with no head: he does not crave and does not chase. Wherever he sits, you are said to loosen your grip and care less.

They spend about a year and a half in each sign, so a change of sign is one of the bigger turning points in the sky. For a Leo Moon, this one moves the calm, detached tail off your own sign, which is why it is worth knowing about.

sections.label: What lifts
title: Back to
being yourself.
paragraphs: Since May 18, 2025, Ketu has been on your sign itself, the first house counted from your Moon sign. That house is you: your body, your mood, the way you come across and the way you see yourself. With the headless tail sitting there, the tradition reads a stretch of feeling a little detached from your own life. You may have asked yourself what you really want, or noticed that the things which used to light you up felt quieter. For a sign ruled by the Sun, that can feel strange.

Over the same months Rahu sat opposite, in your house of partners, the seventh house. That house covers marriage, close partnerships and the people you deal with one to one, including business partners. Rahu there is read as a hunger in your relationships: other people taking up a lot of room, unusual people coming in, and a sense of being pulled by what someone else wanted.

On December 5 both leave. The tradition does not say everything changes on a fixed day, but the particular feeling of being one step removed from yourself is read as lifting from then, and partnerships are read as asking less of you. If the last year and a half taught you who you are without the applause, you keep that.

sections.label: What begins
title: Daily work that clicks,
and real rest.
paragraphs: Rahu moves into your house of daily work, the sixth house from your Moon sign. That house covers your routines, your job as you live it each day, your habits, and the people you compete with. In the tradition the sixth is one of the houses where Rahu is read as doing well: the hungry head is said to give an edge over rivals and the appetite to keep going where others give up. Its useful side is drive in the ordinary hours, the kind that turns into results. Its catch is overdoing it, so the habits you build matter as much as the effort.

At the same moment Ketu arrives in your house of rest and far places, the twelfth house. That house covers sleep, retreat, time alone, letting go, and life far from home, including travel abroad. Ketu there is read as a gentle pull away from noise: wanting more quiet, caring less about keeping up, and finding that time on your own does you good. Some people feel drawn to a faraway place; some simply want earlier nights.
Put together, the next chapter is about rhythm. Show up for the daily work, where the effort is read as paying off, and give yourself the rest that the period seems to ask for.

rows.note: Ketu moved onto your sign and Rahu into your house of partners.
A Saturday. Rahu enters your house of daily work and Ketu your house of rest and far places, at the same moment.
Read as a time when steady daily effort gives you an edge, and quiet time recharges you.
Both move on again: Rahu to your house of joy and romance, Ketu to your house of gains and friends.

steps.name: Pick one habit for December
steps.text: This chapter rewards what you do every day more than what you do once. Choose one small habit that serves your work, start it in December, and keep it simple enough to last.

steps.name: Compete with yourself first
steps.text: The edge over rivals is read as real, but it works best when you measure your progress against last month rather than against everyone else. Let the results speak for you.

steps.name: Book the rest
steps.text: Put quiet time in the diary as if it were a meeting: an evening alone, a long walk, a weekend away. The pull toward rest is part of this period, so give it a place.

steps.name: Enjoy being yourself again
steps.text: With the detached tail off your sign, notice what lights you up now. Say yes to the things that feel like you, and let the people close to you meet that version.

faq.q: Is this for my Sun sign or my Moon sign?
faq.a: Your Moon sign. Vedic astrology reads timing from the sign the Moon was in when you were born, which is often different from the Sun sign most people know.

faq.q: Are Rahu and Ketu the same as the north and south node?
faq.a: Yes. Rahu is the Moon's north node and Ketu is its south node. Vedic astrology uses the sidereal zodiac, so the sign they are in can differ from the one a Western chart shows.

faq.q: Does this mean things at work will go my way after December 5?
faq.a: No one can promise that. The tradition reads these eighteen months as a time when steady daily effort counts for more and gives you an edge. What you do with it, and your own birth chart, decide the rest.

note: Dates are US Eastern time. Vedic (sidereal) astrology, read by Moon sign.
